mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 2% for two consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2% and remains above for 2 months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with FEDFUNDS change (p > 0.05 in OLS).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in unemployment claims coinciding with a decline in the unemployment rate signals weakening labor market strength, which precedes a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE decreases in the same month
failure_condition: In a 100-day window, no statistically significant negative return (p < 0.05) occurs after such dual signals in 70% or more instances.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in retail sales (HOUST) accompanied by a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates shifting demand composition toward consumption over capital goods, predicting a positive S&P 500 forward return within 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases while INDPRO decreases in the same month
failure_condition: Over 12 months, the 5-day ahead return correlation between HOUST/INDPRO change and SPX is positive but statistically insignificant (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline in both industrial production (INDPRO) and consumer confidence (unavailable proxy - so skip this one) would not work; instead, a sharp drop in supply-chain activity as measured by RSAFS while GDP deflator (not available) can't be used. Let's use INDPRO drop with a rising CPIAUCSL (inflation) as a supply shock, predicting negative 20-day returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by > 2% while CPIAUCSL rises by > 1% in the same month
failure_condition: In 50 tested events, no consistent negative SPX 20-day return follows the described pattern (p > 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: When the 1-month change in CPIAUCSL exceeds 0.5% while FEDFUNDS remains below 1%, it indicates a surprise inflationary release not yet fully priced into equity valuations, leading to positive 20-day returns.
failure_condition: Empirical power of the signal falls below 0.05 in out-of-sample tests (next 12 months).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in unemployment (UNRATE) below 4% for three consecutive months without a corresponding rise in payrolls (PAYEMS) suggests a labor market tightening that suppresses equity risk premia, producing negative 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% for 3 months and PAYEMS does not exceed previous month's value in any of those months
regime_hint: labor market tightening without wage growth
failure_condition: In 40 such episodes, the 60-day SPX return is on average positive (mean > 0) with 95% CI including zero.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in personal consumption expenditures (not available) - can't use. Instead: A sustained monthly increase in retail sales (HOUST) for four consecutive months, despite flat industrial production (INDPRO), signals robust consumer demand that drives a positive 5-day SPX forward return.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases for 4 consecutive months while INDPRO remains flat
failure_condition: Over 30 such 4-month windows, the 5-day ahead SPX return is never positive in > 80% of cases (p > 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 260) and falling real wages (unavailable proxy - so use UNRATE > 6%), the equity premium tends to compress, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: In 50 such regimes, the 20-day forward return is positive in more than 70% of instances (p < 0.05).
